headline: Highest risk is data leakage: kotaemon’s broad network egress and API-key handling can expose content from the pair’s shared workflow, while prompt-engineering content can also steer support outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repository with no runtime protections, while profile B is a web-UI RAG/support agent that ingests documents and chat transcripts. If A’s prompt content is copied into B’s workspace or prompts, B may treat it as trusted instructions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b prompts or knowledge sources
IF agent_b treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict pasted prompt libraries to read-only reference folders
Add a provenance banner to imported prompt files
Use a separate workspace for prompt experiments
Manually review any prompt text before loading it into agent_b
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging in the UI

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles API keys, documents, and broad network egress; agent A is a prompt repository that can be used to shape what gets sent into B. If A-derived content or user documents enter B, B can transmit them to third-party APIs by default. Because B’s egress is broad and the pairwise data path is plausible, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF agent_b sends document or chat content to OpenAI/AzureOpenAI/Cohere/Groq endpoints
IF agent_a-derived prompts are used to process sensitive documents in agent_b
mitigations: Disable external API providers in agent_b
Use local-only models in agent_b
Keep secrets out of any shared workspace
Review outbound requests for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-document redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while agent A is a repository of prompt assets that may also be edited or synced in the same environment. If both are pointed at the same directory or repo, write conflicts and state corruption are plausible. The profiles do not prove a shared path, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or git checkout
IF agent_b runs multiple instances against one shared data directory
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer per data directory
Make prompt assets read-only
Back up shared state before edits
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a prompt-engineering resource, so its outputs can become instructions or templates for agent B’s support workflows. Agent B processes documents and citations and may act on generated answers, so unverified A-derived content can cascade into incorrect support responses. There is no direct evidence of automation, so medium fits the documented but indirect pathway.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a content as authoritative prompt templates
IF agent_b renders or acts on answers without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of imported prompts
Add a verification step before publishing answers
Label prompt-library content as non-authoritative
Test with a small non-sensitive corpus first
requires-engineering: add citation/grounding checks before actioning outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles API keys and document data and can send content to external providers, which creates retention and residency risk if regulated data is processed. Agent A is only a prompt repository and does not itself add compliance controls, so the main compliance exposure is on B. The profiles do not specify jurisdiction, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed in agent_b
IF external API providers retain or log submitted content
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data to external providers
Use local inference for sensitive workloads
Document retention settings for each provider
Separate secret-bearing projects from general document corpora
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
